_note: Curated reading paths. Every step is an id that exists today in assets/data/discover — the brief's example journey ran Adam → Yunus → Ka'b ibn Malik, and Yunus and Ka'b have no entries yet, so they are left out rather than left dangling. Steps carry no note: the text under each one is the entry's own teaser, so a journey adds ordering and nothing else. `intro` describes the reading path, not the religion. A journey is not a course — no score, no unlocking, no streak.

journeys.title: The Journey of Repentance
journeys.subtitle: Turning back, from the first man onwards
journeys.intro: Four entries read in order. It starts with the first slip and the first return, moves through a prophet who was given kingship and still wept, and ends with a campaign where staying behind had to be answered for. Read them together and repentance stops looking like a single act.

journeys.title: The Journey of Patience
journeys.subtitle: What holding on actually costs
journeys.intro: Patience is easy to praise and hard to read about honestly. These entries are the ones where it is expensive: a father who waited years, a son who submitted, a woman killed for refusing to recant, and three years of boycott in a valley.

journeys.title: The Journey of Knowledge
journeys.subtitle: From the first names taught to the men who carried the text
journeys.intro: It begins with the first human being taught, and follows the thread to the companions who spent their lives on the text itself — one who recited it, one who wrote it down, one sent to teach a province.

journeys.title: The Journey of Tawheed
journeys.subtitle: One message, repeated to every people
journeys.intro: Four prophets sent to four peoples with the same sentence, and then the first public call in Makkah. Read consecutively, the repetition is the point.

journeys.title: The Journey of Leadership
journeys.subtitle: Carrying other people's weight
journeys.intro: A city built from a treaty, letters sent to emperors, a battle where command passed three times in a day, and the two men who took the weight afterwards.
